Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexlify Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. There will be a brief pause while we poll for questions. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to Nexlify's Second Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hayes, CEO; Sarah Jenkins, CFO; Dr. Elena Vasquez, CTO; Mike Thornton, Chief Revenue Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Product Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Emily Grant, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Hayes.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Nexlify's performance for the second quarter of 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our Nexlify Copilot and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: operating expense breakdown, cash runway, new customer acquisition, gross margin, MRR trends, NRR performance, capital allocation, and operating margin.

These areas highlight our disciplined approach to scaling efficiently in the enterprise collaboration and AI-powered analytics SaaS market. I'll turn it over to Sarah to walk through the financial details across these priorities.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss the financials in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, Jordan. As Jordan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $250 million, representing a 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $70 million.

Let me start by expanding on our gross margin performance, which continues to exemplify the scalability of our asset-light SaaS model. For Q2 2024, our GAAP gross margin stood at 82.3%, marking a 310 basis point improvement from 79.2% in Q2 2023. Excluding about $4.2 million in amortization from our prior Streamline Analytics acquisition, our non-GAAP gross margin hit 83.1%, up 280 basis points year-over-year. For the first half of 2024, GAAP gross margin reached 81.7%, expanding 420 basis points from the prior year, with non-GAAP at 82.9%. This extends our streak of 11 straight quarters of expansion as we grow beyond $850 million in ARR.

The biggest driver was infrastructure efficiencies, contributing roughly 220 basis points. With our customer base up 28% year-over-year to 4,200 enterprise accounts—primarily in financial services and healthcare—we optimized hyperscaler commitments. We boosted AWS reserved instances by 35% and shifted 15% of workloads to Azure's cost-effective sovereign clouds, dropping blended hosting costs per seat by 18%. Our proprietary data tiering engine routes low-latency queries to edge compute and cold data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive, amplifying leverage similar to Snowflake's consumption optimizations.

Product mix added another 140 basis points, thanks to a shift toward high-margin enterprise upsells. Our NRR held at 118%, but Nexlify Enterprise Edition deals with GenAI copilot for sales forecasting now make up 62% of bookings, up from 54%, with margins over 95%. We're prioritizing $500K+ deals over SMB self-serve, echoing Salesforce's Einstein focus.

By region, North America at 68% of revenue delivered 84.5% margins from scale advantages. EMEA improved to 82.1%, up 400 basis points with GDPR localization. APAC, at 14% of revenue after 55% growth, hit 78.9%—up 250 basis points—but reflects data center buildouts in Tokyo and Singapore; we expect convergence soon.

Headwinds were minor, about 50 basis points, mainly from a 12% ramp in GPU costs for Nexlify Insights AI using NVIDIA H100s, pressuring product margins slightly. We've countered with three-year GPU discounts at 22% off and 40% migration to fine-tuned Llama 3 on TPUs. FX shaved 30 basis points from USD strength against Euro and Yen, offset by local currency hedges.

Ahead, we anticipate 200-300 basis points of annual expansion in 2024, targeting 83-84% non-GAAP, via AI support automation cutting headcount 25%, no-code onboarding slashing time-to-value 40%, and serverless shifts like Datadog's.

Next, operating margin came in at 28.2%, up 310 basis points sequentially from Q1's 25.1% and 620 basis points year-over-year from 22%. Operating income hit $70.4 million on $250 million revenue, up 52% YoY. Our Rule of 40 score reached 68—35% growth plus 33% FCF margin—surpassing peers.

Gross margin strength added 72 basis points, from ARM instances on AWS Graviton and Google TPUs cutting compute 25-30%, plus self-service reducing pro services to 9% of revenue. S&M leverage contributed 420 basis points, with expenses up 22% to $85 million or 34% of revenue, down from 38%; CAC payback at 16 months, LTV/CAC 5.2x, NRR 128% from AI upsells. R&D efficiency added 180 basis points, up 28% to $52 million or 21% of revenue, with 40% on GenAI like ForgeAI Agent cutting MTTR 60%; India hubs boosted productivity 15%. G&A at 7% provided a 50 basis point tailwind.

One-offs like $8 million in FX and EU AI Act costs trimmed adjusted margin to 29.8%. For Q3, expect 29-30%, FY24 at 27-28%.

Turning to operating expense breakdown for the first half of 2024, we delivered strong leverage while investing in growth. Total non-GAAP op ex was $428 million, up 18% YoY or 86% of revenue—down 400 bps as we scale toward Rule of 40 at 68% with 32% growth and 36% adjusted op margin.

R&D at $132 million, up 28% YoY or 26% of revenue (up 200 bps), funds differentiation: 35% or $46 million to GenAI like Nexlify Copilot for no-code automation, lifting NRR 15% to 118%; custom models on AWS Bedrock. Headcount to 450 engineers on Kubernetes microservices, zero-trust, with Copilot cutting cycles 20%. Regional: 60% US (SF/Austin), 25% EMEA (London/Tel Aviv for GDPR AI), 15% APAC (Singapore for Japan localization). Expect stabilization at 22-24% in FY24, like Datadog's pivot.

S&M at $210 million, up 14% or 42% of revenue (down 500 bps), with CAC payback 16 months, LTV:CAC 4.2x, Magic Number 1.1. Shift to PLG/digital (55% pipeline via Drift/Marketo), partners like AWS/MS drove 28% new ARR. $85 million to 180 reps for mid-market (45% growth), ABM for CISOs/CROs at 3.5x ROI, events $120M pipeline. Regions: 70% US, EMEA +40% DACH, APAC +35%. To dip below 40% FY24 like HubSpot.

G&A $86 million, up 11% or 17% flat, with 25% headcount to 320 via Workday/Expensify. Legal up 15% to $12M for AI audits/SOC2, IT savings $4M from Salesforce/NetSuite. 65% US, 20% EMEA Dublin, 15% APAC. Op ex growth 12-15% FY24, EBITDA to 28% ahead of Asana/Monday.com.

On new customer acquisition, we added 1,450 net new customers in Q2, up 28% YoY from 1,130 and 12% sequentially from Q1's 1,290. This drove $18.2 million new ARR, up 32% YoY ($1.52 million new MRR), at $12,600 ACV (+9%), 22% of $285 million ending ARR for 24% growth ahead of peers.

Enterprise: 42 net new >$100K ACV (+50%), displacing Jenkins/GitLab. Mid-market 620 (+35%) via freemium 18% conversion. SMB 788 (+22%). NA 68% (980, $12.4M), EMEA 22% (+ from 18%, $3.9M), APAC 10% ($1.9M). Drivers: AI onboarding wizard (45% self-serve boost), 150+ integrations (Kubernetes/Terraform), ABM 3.2x ROI, sales $1.8M ARR/quota. Q3: 1,600-1,750 adds, $20M+ ARR.

MRR ended at $45.2 million, +28% YoY from $35.1 million, +8.4% QoQ from $41.7 million ahead of 7-8% guide. Waterfall: $4.8 million new from 342 logos (ACV $140K, 62% multi-year); $5.1 million expansions (+12% seq, NRR 115%) from AI CodeGuard (28% attach, $3.2M top customers); -$1.7 million churn/downgrades (4.1% gross churn, lowest ever). NA $27.1M (60%, +30%), EMEA $11.3M (25%, +25%), APAC $6.8M (15%, +42%). AI turbocharges, macro resilience, path to $200M ARR FY25.

NRR at 115% dollar-based, down slightly from Q2 118% but above 110% target and peers. Expansion +22% from AI Workflow Intelligence ($18M ARR, 35% adoption, Fortune 50 upsells, CSRD add-on EMEA); contraction -3% (mitigated workshops); churn -4% logo 1.8% (SMB losses offset). NA 118%, EMEA 112%, APAC 108%. Initiatives: AI roadmaps, pricing uplifts, CS Pods targeting 120% Q4.

Cash position ended at $452 million in cash, equivalents, and short-term investments, +$28 million seq from $424 million, +15% YoY from $393 million. Unrestricted $312 million, rest yielding 4.8% ($5M interest). No debt, OCF $32 million (+45%), FCF $28 million (10% revenue). Indefinite runway; conservative 25+ months at old $18M burn. Project $550 million YE, for M&A/share buybacks ($100M auth). NA DSO 52, EMEA 58 improving, APAC +55% ARR despite FX. $50M H2 for SuccessAI (92% churn predict, 25% expansion). Insulated by $620M RPO.

Capital allocation prioritizes ROI: organic 42% OCF ($78M Q3-like) to R&D (Dynacore AI Fabric $25M, 35% query uplift); regional (NA verticals $15M CAC<14mo, EMEA €12M Frankfurt, APAC $10M NTT). M&A $320M YTD: VectorMind $210M (graph AI, 8x ARR), Syncara $65M (no-code), ApexData $45M (APAC). Buybacks $112M (7.2x EV/FCF). 2025: $600-800M (45% R&D, 30% M&A, 15% buybacks).

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.05 billion to $1.08 billion.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for a technology update.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Lisa Chen will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Elena. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of SuccessPredict. This new feature significantly improves churn prediction accuracy to 92%, integrating seamlessly with Snowflake and Databricks. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 41% increase in website traffic and a 35% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Emily Grant:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences and this quarter, we focused on improving our customer support and onboarding processes. As a result, we have seen a 25% increase in customer satisfaction scores.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of Nexlify Copilot on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

Mike Thornton:
Thanks, Ben. Nexlify Copilot has been a game-changer, contributing over 20% to our Q2 revenue growth through upsells and new logos, directly adding $15 million in expansion ARR. Attach rates are hitting 28% among enterprise customers, exceeding our initial 20% target by 40%, with early adopters seeing 15% NRR uplift. Compared to expectations, it's accelerating faster due to viral internal adoption. The landscape includes players like Slack AI and Salesforce Einstein, but we're gaining share in collaboration analytics. Our differentiation lies in proprietary GenAI workflows trained on enterprise datasets, agentic automation, and zero-trust security, paired with AWS Bedrock for cost efficiency—positioning us as the Slack-Snowflake hybrid.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Laura Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Jordan Hayes:
Great question, Laura. International expansion is core to our strategy, with APAC as a priority given its 55% YoY ARR growth. Plans include ramping our Singapore hub, localizing for data sovereignty, and expanding partnerships with Alibaba and NTT. Key targets are Japan for fintech, India for PLG mid-market, and telcos like Singtel. We expect 3-4x ROI over 24 months, mirroring EMEA's trajectory, from shortened cycles via channels driving 30% regional growth. Challenges include regs like Japan's data laws and FX volatility—we're addressing with localized teams, GDPR-like compliance, and natural hedges, confident in 35%+ APAC contribution by FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan.

David Kim:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Sarah Jenkins:
Thanks, David. Churn management remains proactive amid macro pressures. Gross dollar churn is at 4.1%, down 90 bps YoY, with logo churn 1.8%. NRR trends steady at 115-118%, resilient above peers. Strategies include ML-powered Forge Health dashboards reducing multi-month churn 22%, Value Realization Workshops recovering 40% downgrades, and dedicated Expansion Pods. Pricing changes—value-based tiers with 15-20% uplifts on AI—have no negative churn impact, actually boosting expansions 25%. Long-term NRR target is 120% by FY25, driven by AI agents and 92% renewal rates.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with Barclays.

Rachel Lee:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Sarah Jenkins:
Sure, Rachel. CAC averaged $45,000 in Q2, flat YoY but down 10% sequentially as PLG scales, with digital channels now 55% of pipeline. Payback periods improved to 16 months from 20, reflecting higher ACV at $12,600 and 4.2x LTV:CAC. Enterprise deals payback in 12 months, mid-market 18; efficiencies from ABM 3.2x ROI and partners keep us ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Jordan Hayes for closing remarks.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
